lines.japanese: 「まァ、妹萌え選んだってのも予想通りだったなァ。サンプルとしては役に立たなかったよ、御苦労さん」
lines.english: “Well, you choosing the little-sister one was just as predictable as I thought. Useless as a sample, though. Thanks for nothing.”

lines.japanese: 「……おい、ちょっと待て。いま並べられた三冊、どれも妹モノじゃないか」
lines.english: “...Hey, wait. All three books you put out were about little sisters!”

lines.japanese: 「おっはよーっ！　なになに二人で集まって、面白いこと？　私も混ぜて」
lines.english: “Morning! What's this, you two huddled together doing something fun? Let me in.”

lines.japanese: 「げえーっ！　渡来明日香！」
lines.english: “Gah! Asuka Watarai!”

lines.japanese: 「さっきから楽しそうだよね。私もいいかな」
lines.english: “You've sounded like you're having fun for a while. Mind if I join you?”

lines.japanese: 「うほおーっ、山科さんのひとまで！　ちょ、ちょ待ってくれ！　今は、今はよくないっ！　出直してくれっ！」
lines.english: “Uhoh! Even Yamashina's here! W-wait! Wait a second! Now's bad! Now's really bad! Come back later!”

lines.japanese: だが、女生徒二人は俺の制止も聞かず、机の上にあるものを見て絶句していた。
lines.english: The two girls ignored my attempts to stop them, saw what lay on the desk, and fell speechless.

lines.japanese: いつものはちゃめちゃトークでもごまかせそうにない空気が漂っていた。明らかに冷めた表情。
lines.english: Even my usual madcap patter couldn't smooth over the mood. Their faces were visibly cold.

lines.japanese: 「ち、違うぞ？　これはこっちの不良年長者が勝手に用意したものでね？　俺のものじゃないんだよ？」
lines.english: “Th-this isn't what it looks like. This older troublemaker brought them all on his own. They aren't mine, okay?”

lines.japanese: 「あァ、もう成人向漫画は極めた。それ全部おまえにやるよ」
lines.english: “Oh, I'm already done mastering adult manga. You can have all of those.”

lines.japanese: 「極めんの早くね？」
lines.english: “That was fast!”

lines.japanese: 「あーははは……まあ、べつに、うちらカンケーないしねえ？　べつにぱね田くんがロリコンでも気にしないよ」
lines.english: “Ahahaha... Well, it has nothing to do with us, right? I don’t care if Paneda has a Lolita complex.”

lines.japanese: 「だから俺のじゃないって」
lines.english: “I told you, they aren't mine!”

lines.japanese: 「思いやりがあればロリータ・コンプレックスも、ひとつの愛の形だと思うよ。でも、ごめん……私は狭量で視野狭窄な人間だから、受けいれてあげることはできないな」
lines.english: “Provided there is compassion, I believe a Lolita complex can be one form of love. But forgive me... I am narrow-minded and blinkered, so I cannot accept you as you are.”

lines.japanese: 「だから違うんだよおおおぃ」
lines.english: “I told you, you're wrooooong!”

lines.japanese: 「俺は悪いことだとは思わないな。むしろ興味をそそられる素材だね。応援するよ、ロリィー田」
lines.english: “I don't think it's wrong. In fact, it makes you a more intriguing subject. You have my support, Loli-da.”

lines.japanese: 「うまいことでも言ったつもりか」
lines.english: “You think that's clever?”

lines.japanese: 「とりあえず先生来る前にさっさとしまっちゃいなよロリ田くん」
lines.english: “Just put them away before the teacher comes, Lolineda.”

lines.japanese: 「でも触りたくないから手伝いは出来ないよ。ごめんねロリ田くん」
lines.english: “I don't want to touch them, so I can't help. Sorry, Lolineda.”

lines.japanese: 「ああそんな、気を使わなくていいよ渡ロリさんにペド科さん」
lines.english: “Don't trouble yourselves, Wataloli and Pedoshina.”

lines.japanese: その後しばらく羽田班の間には、お互いの名前に「ロリ」を付けるという遊びが流行った。
lines.english: For some time after that, the Haneda Group amused itself by inserting “loli” into one another's names.

lines.japanese: で、昼休み。今日も俺の机の周りにはやる気のない連中がのろのろと集まってくる。
lines.english: Then came lunch. Once again, the usual unmotivated crowd slowly gathered around my desk.

lines.japanese: 今日は高内昌子がいないみたいだ。いつもの面子と外へ食べに行ったのかな。まあ渡来明日香はともかく、山科京や針生蔵人とはノリが合わないのかもしれない。
lines.english: Masako Takauchi didn't seem to be here today. Maybe she'd gone out to eat with her regular crowd. Watarai aside, perhaps she simply didn't click with Kyou Yamashina and Kuroudo Hariu.

lines.japanese: 「針生さんは旅行好きだよね。いいなあ、私も出席日数をもっと稼いでおけばよかったよ」
lines.english: “You really love traveling, Hariu. I'm jealous. I should've built up more days of attendance while I had the chance.”

lines.japanese: 話題を切りだしたのは山科京。しかし学級委員として見逃せない問題発言をしてくれるじゃないか。
lines.english: Kyou Yamashina had raised the subject. As class representative, however, I couldn't overlook a remark like that.

lines.japanese: 「ははは、いけないなあ山科さん。それじゃまるで、学校さぼるのを前提としてるみたいじゃないか」
lines.english: “Hahaha. Now, Yamashina, that makes it sound as though you're planning to skip school.”

lines.japanese: 「うん、その通りだよ」
lines.english: “Yes. That's exactly right.”

lines.japanese: 「こらっ。授業に出ないなんてとんでもない。世界の羽田はそんなこと許しませんよ」
lines.english: “Hey! Missing class is unthinkable. The world-famous Haneda will not allow it.”

lines.japanese: 「そうだよ先輩、出席日数やばいんじゃないの？」
lines.english: “Exactly. Isn’t your attendance in serious trouble?”

lines.japanese: 「知らね。数えたことねえし」
lines.english: “Dunno. Never counted.”

lines.japanese: 「こらこら、まさか留年するなんて言わないだろうな。そんな事実は認めないぞ。あとひとが叱ってるときは、ちゃんと相手の目を見なさい」
lines.english: “Now, now. Don't tell me you intend to repeat the year. I refuse to acknowledge such a reality. And look people in the eye when they're scolding you.”

lines.japanese: 「さあ、卒業できるかなんて教員の連中じゃなきゃ分かんねえし……ン、ンッ、べつに留年することには抵抗ないねえ。ダブリも三ダブも同じようなもんでしょう」
lines.english: “Hell if I know whether I'll graduate. Only the teachers know that... Ahem. I don't mind repeating a year. One year or three, what's the difference?”

lines.japanese: 「俺ァ、あと１０年は学生続けたいんだ。決まった枠の中でしか学生で居られないなんてつまんねえと思わないか」
lines.english: “I'd like to stay a student for another ten years. Don't you think it's boring that they only let you be one inside some fixed little window?”

lines.japanese: 「あ、今のちょっと賛成」
lines.english: “Okay, I kind of agree with that.”

lines.japanese: 「おいおい、賛成じゃないだろ。今この場に居る三名は『羽田班おめでとう！　祝☆卒業小旅行』に参加が義務付けられているんだぞ。勝手に留年なんかするんじゃない」
lines.english: “Hey, don't agree! The three people present are required to attend ‘Congratulations, Haneda Group! Graduation Trip☆Celebration.’ No repeating grades without permission.”

lines.japanese: 「卒業旅行……？　羽田班全員初耳だけど」
lines.english: “Graduation trip...? This is the first anyone in the Haneda Group has heard of it.”

lines.japanese: 「当たり前だ、いま思いついたからな」
lines.english: “Of course. I just thought of it.”

lines.japanese: 俺は鼻息をふんと高く鳴らして、社会の授業で使う世界地図を広げた。
lines.english: I snorted proudly and unfolded the world map we used in social studies.

lines.japanese: 「それでは今から、第一回卒業旅行どこ行っちゃおうか会議を始める。意見がない場合は反論も許さないからそのつもりで」
lines.english: “I hereby call the first meeting of Where Shall We Go on Our Graduation Trip? to order. Anyone without a suggestion forfeits the right to object.”

lines.japanese: 「えっ、私も？」
lines.english: “Wait, me too?”

lines.japanese: 「当たり前だ。それとも山科さん、なにか行けない都合でもあるのか」
lines.english: “Of course. Or is there some reason you can't come, Yamashina?”

lines.japanese: 「ううん、誘ってもらっちゃったと思って。ふふっ」
lines.english: “No. I was just thinking how nice it was to be invited. Heehee.”

lines.japanese: あれ、意外と楽しそう……山科さんのひとは一人が好きそうだけど、意外とみんなでわいわい楽しむのもイケるくちなのかな。
lines.english: Huh. She looked surprisingly excited... Yamashina seemed like the solitary type, but perhaps she could enjoy making noise with a crowd after all.

lines.japanese: 「よし、まずは第一回ということで、行ってみたい場所を好きに挙げていこうか」
lines.english: “Since this is our first meeting, let's begin by naming anywhere we'd like to visit.”

lines.japanese: 「待って。その前に縛り作っていい？」
lines.english: “Wait. Can I impose a few restrictions first?”

lines.japanese: 「縛り？　なんだそりゃ。我が羽田班の旅行につまらない枠組みなど――」
lines.english: “Restrictions? What are those? The glorious Haneda Group's travels need no tedious constraints—”

lines.japanese: 「大自然禁止。アネクメネ禁止。人類未踏地帯禁止」
lines.english: “No vast wilderness. No uninhabited regions. No places untouched by humankind.”

lines.japanese: 「ツンドラは？　樹木限界線を超えた先に広がる凍土を見てみたいな」
lines.english: “What about the tundra? I'd like to see the frozen earth beyond the tree line.”

lines.japanese: 「ボリビア行こうぜボリビア。絶景を見られるいい道があるんだよ」
lines.english: “Let's go to Bolivia. Bolivia. There's a great road with incredible views.”

lines.japanese: 「よし、渡来の意見を採用だ。積極的な発言、素晴らしいぞ」
lines.english: “Good. Watarai's proposal is accepted. Excellent initiative.”

lines.japanese: 「えー」
lines.english: “Boo.”

lines.japanese: 「ファック」
lines.english: “Fuck.”

lines.japanese: 「ぱのひとは？　どこか行きたいとこあるの？」
lines.english: “How about you, Pa? Anywhere you want to go?”

lines.japanese: 「俺か？　ふむ、俺はみんなと出かけられればどこだっていいんだが、遠足的な光景に情景を覚えるなあ」
lines.english: “Me? Hmm. I'm happy anywhere as long as we all go together, but I've always had a soft spot for the whole class-field-trip scene.”

lines.japanese: 「遠足っ！？」
lines.english: “A field trip?!”

lines.japanese: 「えっ、駄目？」
lines.english: “What, is that bad?”

lines.japanese: それまで話半分に聞いてた渡来明日香が、なにか目覚めたかのように顔を上げた。
lines.english: Watarai, who had only half listened until then, raised her head as if something inside her had awakened.

lines.japanese: 「いや駄目とは言ってないよ。なに、遠足案いいじゃん、話してみなよ」
lines.english: “I didn't say it was bad. A field trip sounds great. Go on. Let's hear it.”

lines.japanese: 「あ、うん。俺さ、みんなで山上で弁当を食べたりお菓子を食べたりしたいんだ。健康的で美しいと思わないか」
lines.english: “Okay. I'd like us all to eat boxed lunches and snacks on top of a mountain. Doesn't that sound wholesome and beautiful?”

lines.japanese: 「思う、思うよぱね田くん。それさんせー！」
lines.english: “It does! It really does, Paneda! I vote for that!”

lines.japanese: 「なにっ」
lines.english: “What?!”

lines.japanese: 意外だ。お姫様は山登りなんて嫌いだと思ってたのに。渡来明日香はそれまでのだるだるモードを払拭して、やる気満々面で気焔をあげはじめた。
lines.english: That was unexpected. I'd assumed a princess would hate mountain climbing. Watarai cast off her languid mood, her face blazing with newfound motivation.

lines.japanese: 「おい班長、そういう子供ワードを出すのは卑怯でしょう。こいつそういう……こふっ、子供ワードに弱えんだから」
lines.english: “Hey, Chief, springing kid words like that on us is cheating. She's weak to that kind of... khf, kid stuff.”

lines.japanese: 「私は海外がいいな。ヘルシンキやストックホルムを拠点に、北欧一帯を回りたい」
lines.english: “I want to go abroad. I'd like to use Helsinki and Stockholm as bases and travel all across northern Europe.”

lines.japanese: 「いいねえ。俺は南半球希望だが、今回はそれでもいいや。スピッツベルゲン島まで足伸ばそうぜ」
lines.english: “Sounds good. I was hoping for the Southern Hemisphere, but I'll settle for that this time. Let's go as far as Spitsbergen.”

lines.japanese: 「わあっ、賛成！　聞いてるだけでわくわくするね」
lines.english: “Wow, yes! Just hearing about it is exciting.”

lines.japanese: 「聞いたこともない地名を挙げられて賛成もクソもあるか」
lines.english: “How the hell am I supposed to agree to places I’ve never even heard of?”

lines.japanese: だが二人は俺のツッコミなんか聞いちゃいない。カタカナ地名（それも本国だと正式な名前じゃないとかなんとか文句を垂れていた）を並べたてて、勝手に盛りあがり始めている。
lines.english: Neither of them listened to my comeback. They just kept rattling off foreign place names—grumbling that some weren’t even the official names back home—and getting excited without us.

lines.japanese: 「おい渡来、反撃だ。こっちからも場所を提案するぞ」
lines.english: “Watarai, counterattack. Let's make some suggestions of our own.”

lines.japanese: 「ほいきた」
lines.english: “Roger that.”

lines.japanese: 渡来明日香は地図帳をぱらぱらとめくり、国内における有名観光地をいくつか指差した。
lines.english: Watarai flipped through the atlas and pointed to several famous tourist destinations in Japan.

lines.japanese: 「いやー、いいねえ牧場。やっぱり行くなら高原だねえ」
lines.english: “Ooh, a farm sounds nice. If we're going anywhere, it's gotta be the highlands.”

lines.japanese: 「あ、トナカイの牧場？　楽しそうだね」
lines.english: “Oh, a reindeer farm? That sounds fun.”

lines.japanese: 「温泉もいいなあ。卓球台なんかあったら、朝までラケット振りまわしちゃうね」
lines.english: “Hot springs would be great too. If they had a ping-pong table, I'd swing a paddle till dawn.”

lines.japanese: 「レイキャビクにいい温泉あんだよ。足伸ばしていってみるか」
lines.english: “There's a great hot spring in Reykjavík. We could make the trip.”

lines.japanese: カタカナの地名を並べて、あっちがいいこっちがいいと話しているクラスメイトを他の連中はどう思っていただろう。
lines.english: I wondered what everyone else thought as our classmates tossed around strings of foreign place names and debated where to go.

lines.japanese: 結論は出ないまま、昼休みの時間は過ぎていった。まあいい、今日は第一回の会議だからな。卒業までに決めてやるさ。
lines.english: Lunch ended without a decision. That was fine. This was only our first meeting. We'd settle it by graduation.

lines.japanese: 「いや待てよ。卒業旅行ってことは、卒業しなくちゃいけねえのか。どうすっかな」
lines.english: “Wait. If it’s a graduation trip, does that mean I have to graduate? What am I gonna do?”

lines.japanese: 「卒業くらいはしようよ……」
lines.english: “Could you at least graduate...?”

lines.japanese: いや、早めに決めておいた方がいいかもしれない。一人のクラスメイトの将来がかかってるからな。
lines.english: Perhaps we should decide sooner rather than later. One classmate's future was riding on it.
